rv.q: Dratwa’s moving, clever work unfolded, skillfully and compassionately depicting the messy, difficult business of family relations.
Dirty Laundry most benefits from a top-shelf cast.
Whatever the reason, she has produced an unusually uninvolving play.
Dirty Laundry was incredibly moving, interesting, and engaging, especially in the way it smoothly crossed genres and ideas.

cn.t: Dratwa's moving family drama about grief, infidelity, and unspoken truths earns mostly positive reviews for its compassionate storytelling and clever Greek chorus structure, though some find elements pretentious.
